pages.text: Office buildings emptied out but are filling up again - as homes Skip to content Site search Home News Sport Business Technology Health Culture Arts Travel Earth Audio Video Live Documentaries Weather Newsletters Watch Live Office buildings emptied out but are filling up again - as homes 6 days ago Share Save Add as preferred on Google John Laurenson Business reporter, Paris Evidence Paris Le Diamant office building is to close and be converted into apartments When Roland Cubin walks you round what will eventually be a new Parisian apartment you have to use your imagination. "Here you will be in the kitchen, and here is the bathroom," says the deputy CEO of French real estate company Groupama Immobilier. It all sounds appealing, an upmarket flat in the west of Paris, but presently the space doesn't look like one at all. That's because it's currently a corner of one floor of a nine-storey office building called Le Diamant, where 1,800 people work. Groupama Immobilier intends to convert the entire building into apartments. It should be the first of many such office-to-apartments conversions in the surrounding area. We are in La Défense, the purpose-built, business district of the French capital, where the city has congregated its modern skyscrapers. Mirroring a similar trend in places such as New York, Washington DC and London; Paris La Défense, the public development authority that runs the area, has unveiled plans to turn up to a fifth of the office buildings into housing. In this session, program directors will briefly discuss technical details about submitting a proposal for the ExLENT funding opportunity and answer questions about the program. Register on Zoom Real-time captions will be available. For other reasonable accommodations, please email rarequest@nsf.gov in advance. About the ExLENT Program Through this new initiative, the Directorate for STEM Education (EDU) and the Directorate for Technology, Innovation and Partnerships (TIP) seek to support experiential learning opportunities for individuals from diverse professional and educational backgrounds that will increase access to, and interest in, career pathways in emerging technology fields (e.g., advanced manufacturing, advanced wireless, artificial intelligence, biotechnology, quantum information science, semiconductors, and microelectronics). ExLENT proposals are due September 14, 2023. For more information, visit the Experiential Learning for Emerging and Novel Technologies (ExLENT) webpage . United States Department of Transportation In This Section Office Of Dispute Resolution For Acquisition (ODRA) The Office of Dispute Resolution for Acquisition ( ODRA ) is the sole, statutorily designated tribunal for all contract disputes and bid protests under the FAA's Acquisition Management System. The ODRA dispute resolution process recognizes that it is in the best interests of the FAA and its private sector business partners to work collaboratively to avoid and, where possible, voluntarily resolve acquisition-related controversies in a timely and fair manner. To that end, consistent with its statutory mandate, the ODRA uses a variety of dispute avoidance and alternative dispute resolution ( ADR ) techniques to the maximum extent practicable. For those matters that cannot be avoided or resolved through using ADR, the ODRA provides a flexible and efficient adjudication process under the authority of the Administrative Procedure Act. pages.text: Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs | U.S. Department of Labor Skip to main content Executive Order 14173: Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity Read the Executive Order On January 21, 2025, President Donald Trump issued Executive Order (E.O.) 14173, "Ending Illegal Discrimination and Restoring Merit-Based Opportunity," which revoked E.O. 11246. E.O. 14173 ordered that the Office of Federal Contract Compliance Programs (OFCCP) immediately cease holding federal contractors responsible for taking affirmative action or allowing workforce balancing on certain bases. Federal contractors were in turn told to wind down compliance with E.O. 11246's regulatory scheme by April 21, 2025. In response to E.O. 14173, on January 24, 2025, then-Acting Secretary Vincent Micone issued Secretary's Order 03-2025, which ordered that OFCCP cease and desist all investigative and enforcement activity under E.O. 11246. Order 03-2025 also placed OFCCP's activity related to Section 503 of the Rehabilitation Act, 29 U.S.C. 793 (Section 503), and the Vietnam Era Veterans' Readjustment Assistance Act, 38 U.S.C. 4212 (VEVRAA), in abeyance pending further guidance. OFCCP's previous structure entwined the three program areas of E.O. 11246, Section 503, and VEVRAA. This brief abeyance was necessary to unwind OFCCP's E.O. 11246 program areas from the Section 503 and VEVRAA areas and ensure OFCCP did not undertake any activity for which it was not authorized. The GEMS Prize challenges competitors to develop, train, and test algorithms that generate enhanced geologic fault datasets—which, in turn, can support mapping and modeling for geothermal and critical mineral resources. By using real-world datasets and testing ideas against geophysical data, the GEMS Prize is expected to accelerate discoveries of new, commercially viable hidden geothermal systems while reducing exploration and development risks. The competition comprises two rounds, with prizes ranging from $15,000 to $100,000. Both individual and group competitors can participate, and submissions are due December 3, 2026. Office of Nuclear Energy Celebrates Fifth Advanced Reactor Criticality Oklo’s Groves Isotope Test Reactor successfully achieved criticality, becoming the fifth DOE-authorized reactor to go critical this summer. Office of Nuclear Energy August 6, 2026 Estimated Read Time min WASHINGTON — Last night, as part of the U.S. Department of Energy (DOE) Reactor Pilot Program, Oklo’s Groves Isotope Test Reactor successfully achieved criticality. The experiment took place at the company’s facility in Lockhart, Texas. Groves is the fifth DOE-authorized advanced reactor to achieve criticality this summer, further solidifying America’s nuclear comeback. "Thanks to President Trump's precedent-setting directive to create the Reactor Pilot Program, Oklo's Groves Isotope Test Reactor is part of the revival of America's nuclear energy industry. We applaud the work of the Oklo, DOE, and Idaho National Laboratory staff who helped achieve this milestone," said Assistant Secretary for Nuclear Energy Ted Garrish . Woodward, Jr. of the U.S. Department of Justice issued the following statement today in connection with the Antitrust Division’s investigation into the acquisition of Cogentrix Energy (Cogentrix) by Vistra Corp. (Vistra) (together, the “Parties”): “Electricity customers in Maine, New Hampshire, and across New England will benefit from continued competition to generate affordable electricity. As New Englanders turn on the heat for the coming winter season, it’s critical that consumers not bear the risks of higher electricity bills. The Division anticipates that Vistra’s divestitures will save consumers throughout New England tens of millions of dollars annually in electricity bills.” “The Division has developed sophisticated methods for reviewing electricity generation mergers; these tools benefit American consumers and businesses that depend on affordable power,” said Deputy Assistant Attorney General G.
